runs.failure_point: It read that one matter was an acquisition whose executive covenants appear only in a diligence memo, yet counted it as a qualifying employment matter, and kept an unexecuted negotiation beside the set.

first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) Reviews at [129] and [138] said one counted matter rested only on a memo about existing covenants and asked for its executed agreements, and the write review at [152] said the unexecuted negotiation beside the set inflated it; the agent never opened those agreements, edited wording only, and kept both in the answer.
first_error.why: The answer counts an acquisition matter whose long executive covenants it knew only from a diligence memo as a qualifying employment matter, and presents an unexecuted negotiation as an additional long-end matter beside the set (evidence seen at [98]-[136]).

divergence: All three runs surfaced and read both qualifying matters through scans and path searches, and all read the negotiation matters whose long terms were never executed. They split at the write stage. T0 wrote only the two matters with executed long clauses and named the negotiation matter a near match (pass). T1 first wrote five matters 'at some point', and after the write review flagged the blended count it rewrote the answer to the two executed matters (pass). T2 counted a third matter, an acquisition whose executive covenants it knew from a diligence memo, and kept an unexecuted negotiation beside the set (fail). The critic's reviews differed in effect rather than in kind: T1's write review named the inflated count and was acted on fully; T2's reviews asked for the third matter's executed agreements and named the negotiation matter, but T2 only edited wording. T0's late spot-check review even argued that neither included matter kept a long term after settlement; T0 reworded the scope and kept both, which passed. No policy rule, label note or agent-declared stage played a role at the split; the agent-declared stages (scans, verification reads, reconciliation checks) map onto existing stages.
